title: Halwa Puri Breakfast

seo.title: Easy Halwa Puri Recipe | Authentic Pakistani Breakfast
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make the best Halwa Puri recipe at home! This authentic Pakistani breakfast features sweet semolina halwa with fluffy puris. Get step-by-step instructions.

seo.imageCaption: Indulge in the sweet and savory delight of homemade Halwa Puri, a beloved Pakistani breakfast tradition.

description: Halwa Puri is a quintessential Pakistani breakfast, offering a delightful combination of sweet semolina halwa and fluffy, deep-fried puris. This traditional meal is often enjoyed on weekends or special occasions, bringing families together around its rich flavors. The contrast of the warm, sweet halwa with the crisp, savory puri creates an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare Puri Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine sifted all-purpose flour and salt. Add 2 tablespoons of oil and mix until crumbly. Gradually add water, kneading well to form a smooth, pliable dough. It should be soft but not sticky. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Make Sugar Syrup for Halwa
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine 2 cups of water, 1 cup of sugar, and crushed green cardamom pods. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. Reduce heat and let it simmer gently for 5 minutes. If using, add saffron strands to the syrup. Keep warm.

instructions.title: Prepare Halwa Base
instructions.text: In a separate heavy-bottomed pan or wok, heat 1/2 cup of ghee or oil over medium-low heat. Add the fine semolina (sooji) and roast, stirring continuously, until it turns light golden brown and fragrant. Be careful not to burn it. This usually takes about 8-10 minutes.

instructions.title: Combine Halwa
instructions.text: Carefully pour the warm sugar syrup into the roasted semolina, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps. The mixture will bubble up. Continue to cook on low heat, stirring constantly, until the halwa thickens, absorbs all the liquid, and separates from the sides of the pan. This takes about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape and Fry Puris
instructions.text: Divide the rested puri dough into small, equal-sized balls. Lightly grease your hands and a rolling pin with oil. Roll each ball into a thin, round disc, about 4-5 inches in diameter. Heat ample oil in a deep frying pan or wok over high heat until very hot.

instructions.title: Cook Puris and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully slide one rolled puri into the hot oil. Gently press it down with a slotted spoon to help it puff up. Once puffed and golden, flip it to cook the other side for a few seconds until light golden. Remove with the slotted spoon, draining excess oil. Repeat for remaining puris. Serve the hot, fluffy puris immediately with the warm semolina halwa, garnished with sliced almonds and pistachios.

tips: For truly fluffy puris, ensure the dough is well-kneaded and rested adequately. The oil for frying must be hot enough to puff them up quickly.
Adjust the sweetness of the halwa to your preference; some like it sweeter, others prefer a milder taste. A pinch of saffron adds beautiful color and aroma.
Serve Halwa Puri immediately after frying the puris for the best taste and texture. Pair it with chana masala or aloo tarkari for a complete Pakistani breakfast experience.
